subject: Follow-up and mitigation: streaming chat latency observed Friday
messages:
From: Kevin Nguyen <kevin@fintechplus.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Live chat streaming lag — observed Friday spike

Jonas,

We started seeing a pretty noticeable instability on our live chat between 09:06–09:14 PT this morning. Multiple customers report 'chunky' responses where tokens arrive in 6–12s bursts; in some cases the stream stalls for ~20s and then resumes. The issue reproduced across west-us region only.

Troubleshooting we did on our side: switched to non-streaming (polling) and latency returned to normal, so workaround exists but breaks our UX. No recent client changes. Traffic is normal for us — nothing that should have triggered a surge.

Can you confirm you're seeing an incident and what immediate steps we can take to protect our users while you triage? We're on a tight schedule for a demo later today.

Thanks,
Kevin
Kevin Nguyen
Head of Platform Reliability
Fintech+

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Nguyen <kevin@fintechplus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat streaming lag — observed Friday spike

Hi Kevin — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We are seeing elevated tail latency on a subset of streaming shards in west-us around the same window and have engineers triaging now.

Short-term guidance (client-side / immediate):
- Switch to non-streaming responses as a fallback: set a short polling interval (500–800ms) to avoid long perceived stalls.
- Reduce per-request max_response_tokens to force earlier chunk flushes while we investigate.
- Implement a client-side 3s 'stream idle' timer: if no bytes arrive within 3s, surface a lightweight retry that toggles to the polling path.
- Prefer regional routing to east-us if your traffic allows it (we can route specific keys).

I'll attach a brief checklist and the temporary server-side config we pushed to reduce chunk aggregation. Those are conservative and reversible. Please confirm if you want us to route your traffic to east-us for the demo window — we can make that change without downtime.

We're treating this as a P1 for affected streaming endpoints and will follow up with a root cause summary.

- Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Team — looping you in so we can coordinate the customer postmortem and remedies. Notes from triage so far:
- Symptom: elevated tail latency and intermittent stalls for streaming responses in west-us, peak window ~09:06–09:14 PT on 2027-05-11.
- Impact: Fintech+ (key customer) reported chunked responses and manual fallback to polling; they had a demo scheduled.
- Short-term mitigation: temporary config to reduce chunk coalescing, offered regional reroute to east-us.

Action items:
1) Evelyn — take lead on the server-side timeline and logs: gather shard-level queue lengths, kernel-selection traces, and autoscaler decisions for the window (SUP-2246).
2) Marissa — draft customer-facing summary and compensation proposal; coordinate with CS/Finance for credit.
3) Jonas — own the external communication and timeline to completion; confirm repairs and ETA for postmortem.

Schedule: let's have a 30-min postmortem meeting 2027-05-13 11:00 PT. Invite will follow. Goal: deliver a concise postmortem to Fintech+ by EOD 2027-05-15.

Thanks — keep notes in the shared drive (link below).

Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Nguyen <kevin@fintechplus.com>, Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@fintechplus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: root cause and long-term mitigations for streaming latency

Hi Kevin, Asha — thank you again for your patience. Apologies for the disruption to your demo window; below is a concise summary of what happened, what we fixed, and the steps we're taking to prevent recurrence.

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: an interaction between a recently-deployed kernel-selection optimization and an autoscaler edge-case that, under particular per-shard queue patterns, allowed requests to pile on a small subset of west-us streaming shards. The result was increased queueing and larger-than-expected chunk aggregation which caused the perceived 'burst' and occasional stalls.
- Scope: affected a subset of streaming shards in west-us only; not all customers. Impact window 2027-05-11 09:06–09:14 PT.

What we did (remediation):
- Rollback: reverted the kernel-selection optimization for west-us within 40 minutes of detection.
- Patch: deployed a fix for the autoscaler decision logic to prevent pile-up on single shards.
- Safeguards: applied a temporary server-side limit on chunk aggregation for streaming to ensure steady byte flow to clients.

What we're doing next (long-term):
- Robustness: adding shard-level circuit-breakers and improved backpressure signals so queuing is surfaced earlier.
- Observability: new metric/alert for chunk-aggregation and per-shard queue skew.
- Routing: smarter routing policy that avoids concentrating similar keys onto a narrow shard subset.
- Testing: end-to-end stress tests for the kernel-selector + autoscaler interaction.

Compensation: Marissa will work with your team on an account credit; initial proposal is 25% credit for usage on May 11 for affected services.

Attachments: postmortem-summary.pdf (concise timeline and technical appendix).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review next week to walk through the postmortem details with your SREs. Please let me know what times work.

Again — very sorry for the disruption. We're committed to making this right and restoring confidence in streaming reliability.

Best,
Jonas Weber
